# h3_k8s_node_pool (Resource)

Manages an additional worker pool (node pool) of a managed Kubernetes cluster (`h3_k8s_cluster`): a group of identical worker nodes with its own size, autoscaling, labels, taints and kubelet settings. `replicas`, `autoscaling`, `labels` and `taint` change in place without touching the nodes; `cpu`, `memory_gi`, `disk_gi`, `max_pods` and `kubelet` change **in place by replacing the nodes of the pool one by one** (rolling); `name`, `cluster_id`, `project_id` and `disk_profile` replace the pool. The `workers` group of `h3_k8s_cluster` is the pool `default` of the cluster: manage it there, not with this resource. Deleting the pool drains its nodes. Import: `<cluster_id>/<name>` (provider default project) or `<project_id>/<cluster_id>/<name>`. Uses API-key (HMAC) access to h3k8s (`api.h3llo.cloud/api/k8s/v3`): the key must list the project; scope `k8s:read` is enough to read, changes and the kubeconfig (admin credentials) need `k8s:write`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The cluster's `workers` are the pool "default" (system workloads).
resource "h3_k8s_cluster" "main" {
  project_id         = var.project_id
  name               = "prod"
  cluster_type       = "PROD"
  kubernetes_version = "v1.35.9"

  workers = {
    replicas  = 3
    cpu       = 4
    memory_gi = 8
    disk_gi   = 50
  }

  # Cluster-wide autoscaler settings; here only the extra pools autoscale.
  autoscaler = {
    enabled                     = false
    expander                    = "least-waste"
    balance_similar_node_groups = true
  }
}

# A fixed-size pool for one workload.
resource "h3_k8s_node_pool" "api" {
  project_id = var.project_id
  cluster_id = h3_k8s_cluster.main.id
  name       = "api"

  cpu       = 8  # in place, rolling replacement of the pool nodes
  memory_gi = 16 # in place, rolling
  disk_gi   = 64 # in place, rolling
  replicas  = 3  # in place

  labels = { workload = "api" } # in place, no rollout

  taint {
    key    = "dedicated"
    value  = "api"
    effect = "NoSchedule"
  }

  kubelet = {
    platform_defaults = true # kube-/system-reserved and eviction thresholds by node size
  }

  # Follow the control plane: upgrading the cluster upgrades the pool.
  kubernetes_version = h3_k8s_cluster.main.kubernetes_version
}

# An autoscaled pool that can scale to zero: leave replicas unset.
resource "h3_k8s_node_pool" "batch" {
  project_id = var.project_id
  cluster_id = h3_k8s_cluster.main.id
  name       = "batch"

  cpu       = 16
  memory_gi = 64

  autoscaling = {
    enabled                          = true
    min_size                         = 0
    max_size                         = 10
    scale_down_unneeded_time         = 10
    scale_down_utilization_threshold = "0.5"
  }

  taint {
    key    = "batch"
    effect = "NoSchedule"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) ID of the `h3_k8s_cluster`. Changing it replaces the pool.
- `cpu` (Number) vCPU per node (2-128). Changed in place by a rolling replacement of the pool nodes.
- `memory_gi` (Number) Memory per node, GiB (2-512; 1-16 GiB per vCPU). Changed in place (rolling).
- `name` (String) Pool name: 1-20 characters, lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter. Nodes get the label `h3k8s.io/node-pool=<name>`. Changing it replaces the pool.

### Optional

- `autoscaling` (Attributes) Cluster autoscaler bounds of this pool; changed in place. Removing the block or `enabled = false` turns autoscaling off and the pool keeps `replicas` nodes. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--autoscaling))
- `disk_gi` (Number) System disk per node, GiB (40-400); platform default when omitted. Changed in place (rolling).
- `disk_profile` (String) `replicated` (default, network storage) or `local` (local disk of the host; offered only where the platform enables it). Changing it replaces the pool.
- `kubelet` (Attributes) Kubelet resource reservations of the pool nodes; changed in place (rolling). Removing the block removes the reservations. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--kubelet))
- `kubernetes_version` (String) Kubernetes version of the pool nodes. A new pool runs the control plane version, and an upgrade of `h3_k8s_cluster` upgrades every pool, so usually leave it unset or set it to `h3_k8s_cluster.<name>.kubernetes_version`. Setting a newer version upgrades the pool **in place** (`POST .../upgrade`; at most the control plane version, one step at a time); a downgrade is refused at plan time.
- `labels` (Map of String) Kubernetes labels of the pool nodes; replaced as a whole in place (existing nodes are relabelled). Keys in the `kubernetes.io`, `k8s.io`, `h3k8s.io`, `x-k8s.io` and `h3llo.*` domains are reserved.
- `max_pods` (Number) Maximum pods per node (10-250); platform default (110) when omitted. Changed in place (rolling). Removing it keeps the current value.
- `project_id` (String) Project ID (UUID). Defaults to the provider `project_id` (`H3_PROJECT_ID`). Changing it replaces the node pool.
- `replicas` (Number) Number of nodes (1-100), changed in place. Required without autoscaling. With `autoscaling.enabled = true` leave it unset: the autoscaler owns the node count, `replicas` then shows `autoscaling.min_size` and the actual count is `current_replicas` (no drift).
- `taint` (Block List) Taint of the pool nodes (repeatable); the list is replaced as a whole in place. At least one pool of the cluster must stay without `NoSchedule`/`NoExecute` taints for system workloads. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--taint))

### Read-Only

- `billed_replicas` (Number) Nodes billed now
- `current_replicas` (Number) Nodes the pool has now (set by the autoscaler when autoscaling is on)
- `id` (String) `<cluster_id>/<name>`
- `status` (String) Pool status: `READY`, `PROVISIONING`, `SCALING`, `ROLLING_OUT`, `DELETING`, `UNKNOWN`

<a id="nestedatt--autoscaling"></a>
### Nested Schema for `autoscaling`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable autoscaling of the pool

Optional:

- `max_node_provision_time` (Number) Minutes to wait for a new node before the autoscaler gives up (5-60); 15 when omitted.
- `max_size` (Number) Maximum nodes (1-100, >= `min_size`); required when enabled.
- `min_size` (Number) Minimum nodes (0-100); required when enabled. `0` lets the pool scale to zero (another pool must keep at least one untainted node).
- `scale_down_unneeded_time` (Number) Minutes a node must be unneeded before it is removed (1-60); the cluster value when omitted.
- `scale_down_utilization_threshold` (String) Utilization below which a node may be removed, `"0.1"`-`"0.9"`; `0.5` when omitted.


<a id="nestedatt--kubelet"></a>
### Nested Schema for `kubelet`

Optional:

- `eviction_hard` (Map of String) `--eviction-hard`, e.g. `{ "memory.available" = "200Mi" }`
- `kube_reserved` (Map of String) `--kube-reserved`, e.g. `{ cpu = "100m", memory = "1Gi" }`
- `platform_defaults` (Boolean) Platform reservations: `kube-reserved` by node size, `system-reserved` 100m/200Mi, `eviction-hard` `memory.available<200Mi,nodefs.available<10%,imagefs.available<15%`. The maps below override single keys.
- `system_reserved` (Map of String) `--system-reserved`, e.g. `{ cpu = "100m", memory = "200Mi" }`


<a id="nestedblock--taint"></a>
### Nested Schema for `taint`

Required:

- `effect` (String) `NoSchedule`, `PreferNoSchedule` or `NoExecute`
- `key` (String) Taint key

Optional:

- `value` (String) Taint value

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by "<cluster_id>/<name>" (provider default project) or "<project_id>/<cluster_id>/<name>"
terraform import h3_k8s_node_pool.api <cluster_id>/api
```
